meta.description:
Building 1907, 4th Floor, Room number 401.
The training flight is responsible for overseeing formal, ancillary, & AFSC-specific training for squadron personnel. They provide high-level coordination, expertise, and trust to ensure all personnel meet readiness standards for TRANSCOM Alert cycles. The flight tracks and schedules all training to maintain critical mission capability and manages cross-functional training plans, consolidates AFSC requirements, and delivers tailored readiness reporting to Wing leadership.
meta.jhaNotes: No major workplace hazards exist in this area. Ensure personnel are aligning with proper workstation ergonomics and posture and taking adequate breaks to rest eyes and move bodies.

The assembly location will be at the smoke pit/dumpter location outside of BLDG 1907.

meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
Base speed limit is 25 MPH unless otherwise posted.
Be mindful of deer and other wildlife on the installation and ranges
Road conditions advisories can be found on the JB MDL Facebook page or the JB MDL app
- Green: Roads are clear and dry. Use normal operating procedures.
- Yellow: Roads may be wet and/or slippery. Exercise caution and reduce speeds to 5 MPH below the posted speed limit.
- Red: Road conditions are hazardous. Use extreme caution and reduce speeds to 15 MPH throughout the base and 5 MPH in housing and parking lots.
- Black: Roads are extremely hazardous. Only mission essential and required personnel repoaring for duty are authorized to drive on base - use extreme caution!

Mishap, Occupational Injury, and Illness Reporting

selectedModules.title: Hearing Conservation
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train noise-exposed employees annually on the effects of noise, the purpose of hearing protectors, the advantages and disadvantages of various protectors, and the purpose of audiometric testing.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure workers enrolled in hearing conservation understand noise hazard areas, double-hearing protection requirements, and local follow-up actions tied to occupational health evaluations.
selectedModules.notes: Members may be required to complete an annual audiogram, coordinated with Occupational Helath at the 87th Medical Group clinic. Contact the appointment line to sechedule: (866) 377-2778, option 1,2,5,2 or email the org box at dha.jbmdl.mcguire-87th-mdg.mbx.87-omrs-occ-health@health.mil

selectedModules.title: Forklift / Material Handling Equipment
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 35; 29 CFR 1910.178 - Powered industrial trucks
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train powered industrial truck operators in truck-related and workplace-related topics, evaluate performance, and conduct refresher training when unsafe operation, incidents, or workplace changes occur.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use approved lesson plans, hands-on evaluation, and recurring reevaluation before certifying operators. Cover spotter requirements, aircraft proximity rules, and local route restrictions.
selectedModules.notes: Members may be required to complete forklift competency training in line with their AFSC or mission requirements. All training should be coordinated with Port Flight.

selectedModules.title: CPR Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 1
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide CPR and AED training before assignment where required, and refresh qualification before expiration.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure designated responders maintain current certification and understand location and use of local AED assets under the unit mishap prevention program.
selectedModules.notes: Training is required for established mission-ready requirements. SrA Richard Ramos in the CSS is the primary POC for this training and all certifications are maintained by the CPR program and Training Flight.

selectedModules.title: Flight Line Driving
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 24
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide local flight line driving rules, markings, vehicle lighting requirements, restricted areas, and aircraft hazard awareness before granting driving privileges.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use installation or unit-approved training and certification for airfield/fight line operations, to include local speed, spotter, and no-lone-zone requirements.
selectedModules.afTrainingBasis: DAFMAN 91-203 / Aircraft Flight Line – Ground Operations and Activities
selectedModules.notes: Members may be required to complete flightline driving competency training in line with their AFSC or mission requirements. All training should be coordinated with SSgt Roger Lattimore and certification is tracked by the Training Flight.

selectedModules.title: Manual Lifting and Material Handling
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 20
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on proper lifting techniques, team lifting, load assessment, and use of lifting aids to reduce musculoskeletal injury risk.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide verbal and written guidance on manual lifting, lifting devices, and local reporting actions for strain or overexertion symptoms.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Ergonomics and Material Handling Concepts
selectedModules.notes: Manual lifting will be required during cargo preparation, exercise, and field conditions. Utilize proepr lifting form and implement two-person or MHE lifts when appropriate.

selectedModules.title: Fire Protection and Prevention
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; local fire prevention plan
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on fire hazards, reporting procedures, extinguisher locations, evacuation routes, pull stations, and local emergency response actions.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the JSTO and local fire prevention plan to brief workers on work-center fire hazards, alarm reporting, extinguisher use, and evacuation accountability.
selectedModules.notes: Facility Managers and Supervisors must establish and maintain a fire prevention training program through the JSTO so employees understand their fire prevention and protection responsibilities in the work area. This is fulfilled through job safety training and documentation under DAFI 91-202. Review the prevenetion plan with employee when the plan is developed, when responsibilities change, and wehn the plan changes. If extinguishers are provided for employee use, train employees on the general principles of extinguisher use and the hazards of incipient-stage firefighting at initial assignment and at least annually. Train designated users on the specific equipment they are expected to use.
